claims.text: deploy.sh@stage-2 applies, in order: namespace, Secrets (secrets.sh), ConfigMaps db-init/keycloak-realm/api, db+redis+keycloak+mailpit with Services, waits for db Available, migrate Pod, then api.yaml; output deploy.txt shows that order.
kubectl apply leaves an object whose manifest is unchanged as it is, so re-running the steps is safe; -o name prints each object once whether created, configured or unchanged.
claims.source_hint: kubectl apply reference (-o name); deploy.sh comment lines 8-9

claims.text: A container whose env refers to a missing ConfigMap or Secret (or key) is not started (CreateContainerConfigError); a missing configMap volume keeps the Pod from starting.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: ConfigMaps / Secrets (referencing a non-existent ConfigMap/Secret prevents the Pod/container from starting)

claims.text: db, redis, keycloak, mailpit run the same images as docker-compose.yml (postgres:17.6-alpine, redis:8.10.2-alpine, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.7.4, axllent/mailpit:v1.31.3), each a Deployment replicas: 1 plus a Service of the same name.
kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/<name> --timeout=… waits until the Deployment's Available condition is True, or fails after the timeout.
claims.source_hint: kubectl wait reference; kubernetes.io Deployments (Available condition: minimum replicas available)

claims.text: With restartPolicy: Never, the kubelet does not restart a container that exits; the Pod phase becomes Succeeded if all containers exit 0, otherwise Failed.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (restartPolicy; Pod phase Succeeded/Failed)

claims.text: deploy.sh deletes the old migrate Pod, applies migrate-pod.yaml, polls .status.phase once a second up to 300 times until Succeeded or Failed, prints logs and exits 1 unless Succeeded, then applies api.yaml.
migrate-pod.yaml@stage-2: Pod migrate, restartPolicy Never, image ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-migrate:1.0.0, the same tag 1.0.0 as the api image ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:1.0.0 in api.yaml.
An emptyDir volume is created empty when the Pod is assigned to a node, survives container crashes/restarts, and is deleted permanently when the Pod is removed from the node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Volumes (emptyDir: 'safe across container crashes'; deleted when Pod removed)

claims.text: A replacement db Pod gets a new empty emptyDir, so the postgres image initializes a new database and runs the three init scripts again; data written since (e.g. orders) is lost.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io Volumes (emptyDir); postgres image docs (initdb.d runs on empty data dir); db.yaml comment lines 2-4

claims.text: deploy.sh ends with kubectl rollout status deployment/api --timeout=300s | tail -n 1 (prints successfully rolled out), then kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment --all --timeout=600s (Keycloak slowest).
The Services in donhang are of type ClusterIP (no external address); nothing outside the cluster reaches the api at stage-2.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Service (type ClusterIP default: reachable only from within the cluster); api.yaml comment lines 65-67

claims.text: kubectl run NAME --rm -i --restart=Never --image=… -- cmd runs a one-off Pod, attaches to its output and deletes it when it ends; caddy:2.10.0 has BusyBox wget, which sends a GET and prints the body (-O -).
smoke-test.txt@stage-2: migrate 0/1 Completed, api 2 Pods 1/1 Running, db/keycloak/mailpit/redis 1/1 Running; GET http://api:8080/api/v1/products from a temporary Pod returns the 8 seeded products.
Try it: kubectl get deployments -n donhang lists api 2/2 and db, keycloak, mailpit, redis 1/1; kubectl get services lists api, db, keycloak, mailpit, redis, TYPE ClusterIP, EXTERNAL-IP <none>.
claims.source_hint: kubectl get deployments,services -n donhang on the deployed stage-2 backend

claims.text: On the cluster the api's host names (db, redis, mailpit, keycloak) are the same as in Compose: ConfigMap api and Secret api (Host=db) use the Service names.
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-2:deploy/k8s/api-configmap.yaml, stage-2:scripts/k8s/secrets.sh line 30, stage-2:docker-compose.yml

claims.text: In Compose at stage-2 the api publishes no port; the browser reaches it through Caddy, which proxies /api/v1 to api:8080.
claims.source_hint: git -C examples/don-hang show stage-2:docker-compose.yml (web service ports) and stage-2:Caddyfile

claims.text: kubectl get pods shows STATUS Completed for a Pod whose phase is Succeeded (containers exited 0).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Lifecycle (phase Succeeded); kubectl get pods output (Completed)

claims.text: If the migrate Pod does not succeed, deploy.sh prints its log and exits 1 before applying api.yaml, so the api Pods already running are left untouched and keep serving.
